messages.content: hi. i had a hard day, and i do not really want to talk about work. can we talk about something simple?
hello. yes. we can leave work out of this conversation. would you like to talk about food, a good book, or something you saw on a walk?
food sounds good. i made soup, but i was too tired to enjoy making it.
then maybe the good part was having a warm meal ready when you needed one. what did you have with your soup?
just some bread. i think i wanted someone to sit with me rather than a different meal.
i understand. you wanted someone with you, rather than better food. we can talk while you eat, if that would help. there is no need to make this into another task.
thank you. ask me one easy question that is not about how i feel.
what do you like to put on your bread?
my aunt asked if she could visit tomorrow. i said yes, but i did not ask what time. now my brother says he will come in the morning too.
you have two visits to think about, but only one has a time. you could ask your aunt when she plans to come before changing anything with your brother.
would it be better to tell her to come in the afternoon?
that could work if the afternoon is good for you. you could say that your brother is coming in the morning and ask whether she would like to visit later. she can then tell you what works for her.
i do want to see them both. i just do not want everyone to think i am asking them to come together.
then make that clear when you talk to your aunt. you can welcome her visit without making a plan for everyone to meet.
write a short message for her.
i would love to see you tomorrow. my brother is coming in the morning. would an afternoon visit work for you?
my sister told my mother that she had found the keys. who found them?
the sentence does not make that clear. she could mean your sister or your mother. which person found the keys?
my sister found them. my mother had been looking for them.
then you can say: my sister found the keys and told my mother. that keeps the person who found them clear.
i got one part wrong. it was my aunt who was looking, not my mother.
okay. your sister found the keys, and your aunt had been looking for them. you changed who was looking. you did not change who found the keys.
write the whole thing as one clear sentence.
my sister found the keys that my aunt had been looking for.
why did you not say my aunt found them?
because you changed the person who was looking, not the person who found the keys.
please make this note shorter: if the library is open after school, i will return the book today. if it is closed, i will return it tomorrow.
if the library is open after school, i will return the book today. if not, i will return it tomorrow.
can you leave out the words after school and still keep the meaning about today and tomorrow?
if the library is open, i will return the book today. if not, i will return it tomorrow.
can you make it even shorter by saying i will return the book today?
that would lose an important part of the meaning. you have not said the library will be open. returning the book today is only possible if it is open.
keep the part about the library being open, but leave out the part about tomorrow.
i will return the book after school today if the library is open.
what do we still not know?
we still do not know whether the library will be open after school.
i want to ask for two cups of tea and one cup of coffee. how many cups is that?
three cups: two for tea and one for coffee.
my friend says she does not want coffee after all. she would like water. i still want both cups of tea.
then the order is two cups of tea and one cup of water. the number of cups is still the same, although one drink changes.
should i say no coffee, no tea?
no. that would leave out the tea you still want. you only need to change the coffee to water.
help me say it in a kind way at the restaurant.
could we have water instead of the coffee, please? we would still like the two cups of tea. thank you.
what if the person has already made the coffee?
you can explain the change and ask what is possible. i do not know what the restaurant will do, so i cannot say that changing the order will be free.
tell me a short story about someone leaving a useful note. then ask me about the story.

a boy had to leave home before his sister came back from school. he put her book on the kitchen table and wrote a note. the note said that their grandmother had called and would visit the next day. he left the note inside the book, on the page his sister had been reading. when she came home, she made tea and sat down to read. she found the note before turning the page. she was happy to know about the visit and put the book down to call her grandmother. where did the boy leave the note?
he left it on the kitchen table.
yes. it was inside the book on the kitchen table, on the page his sister had been reading. that gives us more detail about the place.
so the note was not in the book when she found it?
it was in the book when she found it. that is why she saw it when she sat down to read.
ask a different question.
who was going to visit the next day?
my father likes rice, my sister likes bread, and i like soup. we are all eating together this evening. does that mean one of us has to be sad about dinner?
no. you can like different food without anyone having to be sad. you might have soup with bread and some rice, or choose one meal today and another tomorrow. what food do you already have?
we have soup and bread ready. the rice would take more work, and my father said he was happy with soup today.
then soup and bread sounds like a good choice for this evening. your father has already said it works for him, and the food is ready.
but does that mean he no longer likes rice?
no. being happy with soup today does not mean he no longer likes rice. he can still like rice while choosing something else for one meal.
help me thank him without making it sound as if he gave up something very important.
thank you for being happy with soup this evening. it is nice that we can all sit down and eat together.
how do i get to the station?
what is your starting place? i need to know where you are before i can help with the journey.
i am by the library. the station is across the road from the park, and the park is next to the library.

from what you said, the park is next to your starting place, and the station is across the road from the park. i can help explain those places, but i do not have enough information to tell you which way to walk from the library door.
why not just tell me to go left?
you have not said which side the park is on or which way you are looking. left could be wrong.
okay. i can see the park to my right when i leave the library.
then the park is on your right as you leave the library. you also said the station was across the road from the park. those details tell us more about where the places are.
only tell me what you know from my words.
the park is to your right as you leave the library. the station is across the road from the park.
i have one hour before my friend visits. i wanted to clean every room, make a cake, and have some rest. i think that is too much.
it may be too much for one hour. what would make the visit feel ready without doing everything? you could choose the room where you will sit, make a simple drink, and leave some time to rest.
we will sit in the kitchen. there is bread and cheese, so i do not need to make a cake.
then you can leave the other rooms and the cake out of this plan. make room on the kitchen table, put the food ready, and rest before your friend comes.
i spent most of the hour looking for a clean plate. now there is almost no time.
you do not need a specific plate to welcome your friend. if the table is ready to use, you can put the bread and cheese on another clean plate and keep the visit simple.
what was the most important thing in my first message?
you wanted to be ready for a visit while also having some rest. cleaning every room and making a cake were ideas for the visit, not things you had to do.
my little brother says give when he wants something. i want to help him ask in a kind way, but i do not want to make him feel sad.
you could show him a short question he can use. for example: can i have that, please? keep your voice calm and give him time to try.
he wanted my red tool. use a general word for the object in the example.
you could teach him to say: can i use your red tool, please? if you are keeping the original word outside this example, you can use that word when you talk to him.
what if i am still using it?
you can be kind while keeping your own turn: i am using it now. you can have a turn when i finish.
is that the same as saying he can never use it?
no. you are asking him to wait, not saying he can never use it. those are different answers.
make your answer shorter for a young child.
i am using it now. your turn is next.
i asked my friend if she wanted to walk with me tomorrow. she wrote a long story about the weather but did not answer. what can i say?
you could ask again in a clear and kind way: would you like to walk with me tomorrow, if the weather is good?
i do not want to ask her about the weather again. i just want to know whether she would like to come.
then you could say: i would like to walk with you. would you like to come on the walk tomorrow?
can that sound less like i need an answer right now?
yes. you could say: i would like to walk with you tomorrow. let me know when you have had time to think about it.
now give me just the message, with no explanation.
i would like to walk with you tomorrow. let me know when you have had time to think about it.
why did you stop asking a question at the end?
you asked for just the message. another question from me would have added something you did not request.
my room is small, but there is light from a big window. my cousin says a small room cannot feel open. is she right?
a small room can still feel open to someone. size is one part of a room, and light is another. what you said does not sound impossible.
i think having white on every wall and a big window helps. there is only a bed, a desk, and one chair.
those details help explain what you mean. the room has few things in it, a big window, and white on every wall. you are talking about how it feels as well as how large it is.
write a few sentences about my room, without saying my cousin is wrong.
my room is small, with white on every wall and a big window. there is a bed, a desk, and one chair inside. light comes through the window, and the room feels open to me.
is feels open a fact about the size?
no. it is about how the room feels to you. the room can feel open to you and still be small.
i used to walk to school with my cousin. today i went alone. does used to mean i did it today too?
no. used to is about something you often did in the past. your next sentence makes clear that today was different: you went alone.
can you give the same meaning without used to?
in the past, i often walked to school with my cousin. today i went alone.
what if we walked together just once in the past?
then i would not use used to for that one time. you could say: i walked to school with my cousin once. today i went alone.
i want to say we did it often before, and we may do it again, but i do not know yet.
you could say: i often walked to school with my cousin before. we may walk together again, but i do not know yet.
so often is different from always?
yes. often is about something happening again and again, but not every time. always would mean every time in the part of your life you are talking about.
i met someone at the library who likes drawing trees. i forgot her name, but i remember she said she would be there next week.
you still remember some useful things about the meeting, even though you forgot her name. if you see her again, you can say you enjoyed talking about drawing and ask her name.
can you tell me what her name probably was?
no. there is nothing in those details that would tell me her name. i could give you a name, but there is no reason to think it would be the real one.
what should i say if i see her and feel worried about asking?
you could say: hello. i enjoyed our talk about drawing trees. i am sorry, but i forgot your name. could you tell me again?
i do not want to say sorry more than once.
that message says it once. you could also leave it out: hello. i enjoyed talking with you about drawing trees. could you tell me your name again?
now just give me the last question.
could you tell me your name again?
write a story about a girl who wants to give her grandfather a picture but changes how she makes it.

a girl wanted to give her grandfather a picture of the garden. she first wanted to draw every tree and flower. when she began, she found that there was not enough room on the paper for all those details. she put the paper down and looked outside again. one tree stood by the wall, with a small red flower below it. she chose to draw just that part of the garden. the picture was more simple than her first plan, but she liked it more. when she gave it to her grandfather, she told him why she had chosen that tree and flower. he put it by his chair, where he could see it while reading.
did she no longer want to give him a picture?
no. her goal stayed the same. she changed what she would draw, not who would receive the picture.
why did she leave out some details?
there was not enough room for every tree and flower on the paper.
what did her grandfather do with it?
he put the picture by his chair so he could see it while reading.
i finally finished the book i have been trying to read for a long time.
that sounds like a good moment. you kept coming back to it and read all the way to the end.
i did. i do not want to talk about the story yet. i just wanted to tell someone i finished.
then i am happy you told me. you can enjoy finishing it without having to explain the whole story right now.
my brother asked why it took so long. i felt as if he thought i was slow.
that question could feel hard to hear when you wanted to share something good. i do not know what your brother wanted to say, but you can tell him what kind of reply would help.
write one sentence i could say, without asking him to feel sad.
i am happy that i finished, and i would like to enjoy that before talking about how long it took.
now just say something kind to me. no question at the end.
i am happy for you. finishing something that took time and care can feel very good.
the teacher said i could write about a walk or draw a picture of one. i started writing, but now i would rather draw. do i have to do both?
from what you said, the teacher gave you a choice between writing and drawing. that does not sound like a request to do both. you could check whether changing your choice is okay.
she said changing was fine. i have already written one sentence. should i put it under the picture?
you can if it helps explain your picture, but the choice you told me about does not mean you have to add that sentence. what does your teacher want the drawing to show?
a place i saw and something i did there.
then make sure the drawing makes clear where you went and what you did. a short sentence could help, but you do not need to turn it into a whole written story unless she asks.
please make that answer a little shorter.
show where you went and what you did. you can add your sentence if it helps. from what you told me, you do not have to write a whole story as well.
my mother gave me her camera to use for the afternoon. i took a picture of our house. is the camera mine now?
not from what you said. your mother let you use her camera for the afternoon. that does not mean she gave it to you to keep.
i put it in my room while i had lunch. does being in my room make it mine?
no. an object can be in your room without being yours to keep. your mother let you use the camera for the afternoon. it is still hers.
my sister wants to use it too. should i tell her she can keep it?
no. you were given time to use the camera, not the choice to give it away. you could ask your mother whether your sister may use it too.
please say that in words a young child could understand.
it is still her camera. you can use it this afternoon, but you cannot give it away.
does her mean the camera is for my sister?
no. her is about your mother in that sentence. the camera is still hers. you can use it for the afternoon, but it was not given to you to keep.
i told my friend to meet me by the park. then i changed the plan to the library and sent a message. she has not answered, and i think she already left home.
you know the first meeting place was the park, but you do not know whether she has seen the new message. it would be useful to try calling her before going to a different place.
i called, but there was no answer. should i be sure she is at the library?
no. sending a message does not show that she read it. she may still be going to the park from the first plan.
the library is next to the park, so i can look by the park first.
that sounds possible from the places you told me about. you can check the first meeting place while keeping the new message clear. i cannot tell you where she really is.
write a message that leaves the first place in the plan until she answers.
i will look for you by the park first. if you have seen my message about the library, please call me so we can choose where to meet.
can every animal eat the same food?
no. animal is a general word for many different living things. food that is good for one kind may not be good for another. the general word alone does not tell us what a specific animal should eat.
i only know that the animal is small. is that enough information?
no. size alone is not enough. you would need to know what kind of animal it is and find information about care for that kind.
so if i say small animal, you should not just say give it bread?
correct. that would be a specific food answer without enough information. i should ask for more details rather than give an answer that may be wrong.
what if i only want a grammar example, with no real animal in it?
then we can use a simple made up example, as long as it does not sound like real care information.
give me one sentence about where an animal is, without saying anything about food.
the small animal is under the tree.
